title: Family of 3 found dead in North Carolina home had been using generator after power was shut off, neighbors say - NewsBreak
text:
By Shanila Kabir ,
16 hours ago
ROCKY MOUNT, N.C. ( WNCN ) — Three people were found dead inside a mobile home due to possible carbon monoxide poisoning on Monday.
The Rocky Mount Police Department found their bodies Monday during a welfare check on King Charles Court at the Kingsway Mobile Home Park.
A mobile home on King Charles Court in Rocky Mount, where three members of a family were found dead. (Shanila Kabir) CBS 17 spoke to the family and neighbors of Tracy and Kenny Swann. They said the Swanns’ power was shut off just days prior.
Thomasville man charged in deadly hit-and-run on Interstate 85 in Guilford County Their son, 24-year-old Kenyan Patterson, is devastated by the death of his parents. He adds that they were kind, hardworking people.
“Tracy was a go-getter. She cared for her kids, and she always made sure there was food in her house. She would give you anything you wanted. That was the kind of people they were,” said Patterson.
Rocky Mount Police found the couple, along with their adopted daughter Mahala, dead inside the mobile home on Monday.
“Mahala was a sweetheart,” Patterson said. “She’d never hurt a soul.”
Neighbors in the Kingsway Mobile Home Park said the family always offered a helping hand, despite going through their own challenges.
“They were really nice people. They bought me vegetables, and they helped me move in and move furniture around. They were just really great people,” said neighbor Mary Thompson.
Neighbor Demetrius Wright said Kenny Swann recently told him he was more than $2,000 behind on the electricity bill.
“He went down there, and they had him pay $1,000, so he paid it. I thought that they would turn the lights back on for consideration, but they didn’t do it,” Wright said. “It forced him to go to his mom’s house and grab a generator to keep the house cool.”
Wright believes that it might have played a role in their death. Kenyan Patterson adds that he had no idea his parents needed extra help.
“Everybody goes through something, and people just need help, even though they might not call out for it. It’s important to check in and make sure. Sometimes people want to believe they can do it on their own, but they really can’t,” said Patterson.
The family’s three dogs were also found dead inside the home.
The North Carolina office of the Medical Examiner is now working to determine the family’s cause of death.
